solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Elegant socialite being broadcast

parts.note: a deb, short for debutante, is a young society woman
a programme being broadcast is on air

explanation.surface: A stylish society figure appears on radio or television.
explanation.definitionFit: Debonair describes a man who is suave, stylish and charming, a synonym of elegant.

clue.text: Very cold beer

explanation.surface: An ice-cold pint of beer.
explanation.definitionFit: Two senses: a bitter wind is freezing, and bitter is a traditional British ale.

clue.text: A grim terribly ancient plant

indicators.note: terribly suggests the letters of a grim are mangled into a new order

parts.note: ancient means old

explanation.surface: A grim, very old plant, as if from a horror garden.
explanation.definitionFit: The marigold is a common garden flower, so it is an example of a plant.

clue.text: Man's first card, a club

indicators.note: first asks for the opening letter of the word Man's

parts.note: an ace is a playing card

explanation.surface: A man's opening card in a game is a club.
explanation.walkthrough: 'card, a club' tempts a solver to read the suit of clubs; club here is a weapon.
explanation.definitionFit: A mace is a heavy club-like weapon with a spiked or flanged head.

clue.text: Show up again to gather fruit

parts.note: to reap is to gather in a harvest
a pear is a fruit

explanation.surface: Someone returns to an orchard to collect the harvest.
explanation.definitionFit: To reappear is to come back into view, a synonym of showing up again.

clue.text: Liquid measure, litre, held by girl, working

indicators.note: held by says the litre letter sits inside the word for girl

parts.note: gal is an informal word for a girl
a machine that is working is on

explanation.surface: A girl at work holds a litre, a liquid measure.
explanation.definitionFit: A gallon is a unit of volume for liquids, eight pints.

clue.text: Ballad about duke and lord's wife

indicators.note: about means the word for ballad goes round the duke's letter

parts.note: a lay is a narrative song or ballad

explanation.surface: A ballad tells of a duke and a nobleman's wife.
explanation.definitionFit: Lady is the title of a lord's wife in the British peerage.

clue.text: This helps one to see in garret (in attic)

indicators.note: in says the letters lie within the words that follow

explanation.surface: Something helps you see inside a dark garret up in the attic.
explanation.definitionFit: The retina is the light-sensitive layer at the back of the eye, essential to sight.

clue.text: Cautious bringing in youth as cleaner

indicators.note: bringing in means the word for cautious takes the youth inside it

parts.note: chary means wary or cautious
a lad is a youth

explanation.surface: A wary employer takes on a young person as a cleaner.
explanation.definitionFit: A charlady is a British term for a woman employed to clean houses or offices.

clue.text: Did battle, reportedly, in old trading station

indicators.note: reportedly means the word for did battle is heard rather than spelt

parts.note: did battle means fought

explanation.surface: Fighting took place, so we hear, at a historic trading post.
explanation.definitionFit: Trading companies in colonial North America and Africa built fortified posts, called forts, as trading stations.

clue.text: In favour of concert being shortened

indicators.note: being shortened says the word for concert loses its final letter

parts.note: a prom is a promenade concert, as at the BBC Proms

explanation.surface: Someone supports a concert being cut down in length.
explanation.definitionFit: Pro is a Latin-derived preposition meaning for or supporting.

clue.text: Man perhaps after fine knitwear pattern

indicators.note: after puts the island word following the word for fine

parts.note: fine weather is fair
the Isle of Man is one example of an isle

explanation.surface: A man perhaps chases a fine knitting pattern.
explanation.walkthrough: Man is the Isle of Man, between Britain and Ireland; Fair Isle is a Shetland island famous for its colourful knitting.
explanation.definitionFit: Fair Isle is a style of multicoloured patterned knitting named after a Shetland island.

clue.text: Photograph game attacked with gun

parts.note: snap is a children's card game
to have shot is to have fired at with a gun

explanation.surface: A picture of game birds being fired upon.
explanation.walkthrough: 'game' looks like hunted birds; it is the card game.
explanation.definitionFit: A snapshot is an informal, quickly taken photograph.

clue.text: Tots turn over

indicators.note: over signals the word for turn is flipped end to end

parts.note: a spin is a turn

explanation.surface: Small children roll over.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Tots' looks like toddlers but means small drinks.
explanation.definitionFit: A nip is a small measure of spirits, as is a tot.

clue.text: In religious house it is something given special attention

indicators.note: In places the word it within the word for a religious house

parts.note: a priory is a monastery or convent run by a prior

explanation.surface: Inside a monastery, one thing gets particular care.
explanation.definitionFit: A priority is a matter treated as more important than others.

clue.text: Helpful hint about river excursion

indicators.note: about means the hint word wraps around the river's letter

parts.note: a tip is a helpful hint

explanation.surface: Useful advice about a river outing.
explanation.definitionFit: A trip is a short journey or outing, a synonym of excursion.

clue.text: Police using bad PR a lot

indicators.note: bad suggests the letters of PR a lot are put into a poor, jumbled order

explanation.surface: The police rely heavily on poor public relations.
explanation.definitionFit: To patrol is to police an area by going round it regularly.

clue.text: Word puzzle bringing on a vexed moment, by the sound of it

indicators.note: by the sound of it means the phrase for a vexed moment is heard, not spelt

parts.note: a vexed one is a cross one, and a moment is a tick, giving a cross tick

explanation.surface: A word puzzle brings on a moment of annoyance.
explanation.definitionFit: An acrostic is a puzzle or poem where initial letters of lines spell a word.

clue.text: Passionate romance captivating millions

indicators.note: captivating means the romance word holds the millions letter inside it

parts.note: a romance is a story

explanation.surface: A passionate love affair that enthrals millions.
explanation.definitionFit: Stormy describes a relationship full of strong feeling, a synonym of passionate.

clue.text: A record for a high mountain

parts.note: an LP is a long-playing record

explanation.surface: A record set for climbing a high peak.
explanation.definitionFit: An alp is a high mountain, especially one in Switzerland.

clue.text: Told to go with group touring North

indicators.note: touring means the group word goes all round the north letter

parts.note: a set is a group

explanation.surface: A band was instructed to set off on a tour of the North.
explanation.definitionFit: Sent means dispatched, which is what someone told to go has been.

clue.text: Emperor in Wagner opera

indicators.note: in says the letters sit inside the words Wagner opera

explanation.surface: An emperor appears in a Wagner opera.
explanation.definitionFit: Nero was a Roman emperor of the first century AD.

clue.text: Fine artist depicting ladies' fingers

parts.note: OK means fine or all right
RA is a Royal Academician, an artist

explanation.surface: A good painter portraying women's hands.
explanation.walkthrough: 'ladies' fingers' looks like a hand to paint but is a vegetable.
explanation.definitionFit: Okra pods are also called ladies' fingers, a name for the same vegetable.

clue.text: I haven't a clue what suspicious customs officer might do

definitions.meaning: an informal expression of complete ignorance

definitions.text: what suspicious customs officer might do
definitions.meaning: taken literally, an official wanting to frisk a traveller would ask to examine their person

explanation.surface: A traveller shrugs off a suspicious customs official.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase is an idiom for not knowing, and literally an invitation to be frisked.

clue.text: Distant meteor disintegrated

indicators.note: disintegrated suggests meteor breaks apart and its letters reassemble

explanation.surface: A faraway meteor burned up.
explanation.definitionFit: Remote means far away, a synonym of distant.

clue.text: Fired back in the course of fight — not with this weapon!

indicators.note: in the course of puts the turned word inside the word for fight

parts.note: a set-to is a fight or scrap

indicators.note: back means the word for fired is read from right to left

parts.note: fired, as a fuse or lamp, is lit

explanation.surface: Someone fired back during a fight, though not with this blade.
explanation.walkthrough: 'back' turns LIT into TIL. The closing 'not with this' is a joke: you cannot fire a dagger.
explanation.definitionFit: A stiletto is a slim, sharp dagger, a kind of weapon.
